title.narrative: PERFORMANCE-BASED PARTNERSHIP SCHEME FOCUSING ON QUALITY PROGRAMMING, UNDERSTANDING CHANGE AND RESULTS FOR POOR HOUSEHOLDS AND COMMUNITIES

description.narrative: The Urban Green Graduation programme will work in Dhaka, Bangladesh. It aims to contribute to Concern Bangladesh’s Green Graduation thematic programme, and the goal of the grant is to ensure households can sustainably meet their basic needs and have improved coping strategies through strengthened livelihoods which place value on the natural environment. The programme will support over 69,870 urban extreme poor people living on pavements or informal settlements including female-headed households and households with disabled members. This will be done through supporting households with start-up capital or asset tranfers, supporting households to meet their basic needs, households engaged with micro-enterprises and improved access to affordable, accessible and appropriate financial services and increased savings.. RM Adaptation 2: With this allocation, the green graduation (GG) programme in Bangladesh will conduct a Climate Vulnerability and Capacity Assessment (CVCA) with the support of Head Office technical advisors. The purpose of the CVCA will be to support LTD GG communities to identify contextual climate shocks, stresses and changes that are impacting their ability to secure their basic needs. Communities will then be supported to develop Community Adaptation Action Plans (CAAPs) to address areas where communities can be empowered to make a positive difference in their resilience at the household or community level. The intention is that elements of these plans will be financed through the Climate Allocation in 2025. DRR 1: Green Graduation programmes are intended to build the resilience of communities and natural systems to a changing climate through awareness raising, capacity building, environmental awareness and promoting climate-smart activities. Aid to Environment 1: Concern’s Green Graduation programme added a 5th pillar to the traditional graduation model - the ‘green’ aspect which aims to improve environmental protection and stability through awareness raising, capacity building, assessing environmental impacts, reducing and managing environmental risks and increasing natural assets. Capacity Building 1: building the capacity of communities on climate-smart activities is necessary for environmental protection and sustainability. Gender Equality 1: a gender lens is applied at every stage and a gender transformative approach is taken to tackle harmful gender norms, attitudes and practices. Nutrition 1: Through improved agricultural practices (increasing yields) and messaging on nutrition, the nutritional status of HHs is improved.
